title: Now: 2028
summary: The AI infrastructure supercycle, advanced chips, and the energy buildout that powers it.
bodyHtml:
📅 This horizon is the most investable. Milestones are well-defined, companies are identifiable, and capital is already flowing at scale. Updated July 2026.

The Big Picture

We are in the early innings of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. AI is the demand driver. Chips, data centres, power, and networking are the supply response. SpaceX just completed the largest tech IPO in history (SPCX). The Hormuz deal is reshaping oil markets. The FOMC is navigating a hawkish pivot. Every milestone below has named companies and stock implications.

Milestones

GB200 NVL72 systems shipping at scale. Each NVL72 rack contains 36 Grace CPUs and 72 Blackwell B200 GPUs drawing 120kW: the single most power-dense compute product in commercial production. TSMC CoWoS capacity expansion is the binding supply constraint. HBM3E from SK Hynix and Micron is the memory critical path.

What it means: NVIDIA's data centre revenue has surpassed its PC gaming revenue permanently. The Blackwell cycle extends the addressable market for advanced packaging (TSMC), HBM memory (MU), and power infrastructure (ETN) simultaneously.

NVDA TSM MU
Confirmed
Leader: NVDA · 90% vs MU 70% · +4 more

First 2nm wafers in high volume production. Apple (iPhone 17 series) and NVIDIA (next-gen Rubin GPU) are the lead customers. N2 delivers approximately 15% power efficiency improvement and 10-15% performance gain over N3E at the same power budget. Gate-all-around transistors replace FinFET for the first time in TSMC's process history.

What it means: TSMC's node leadership gap over Samsung and Intel widens. N2 pricing ($25,000+ per wafer) is premium: TSMC captures more value per chip at each node generation. ASML EUV machines are required for N2; every new N2 wafer start is an ASML consumables event.

TSM ASML AMAT
Confirmed
Leader: TSM · 99% vs ASML 90% · AMAT 78% · +4 more

Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta collectively spending $300B+ per year on AI infrastructure. Power grid permitting becomes the binding constraint in the US: not chip supply. New data centre builds in Virginia, Texas, and the Midwest are limited by transformer availability and grid interconnection queue wait times (2-4 years in some markets).

What it means: Power infrastructure stocks are the most underloved AI derivative. Eaton (ETN) and Quanta Services (PWR) have years of backlog and cannot expand capacity fast enough. The investment case does not require a view on which AI model wins: it requires only that data centres keep being built, which is contractually committed capex.

MSFT ETN PWR GEV
Confirmed
Leader: MSFT · 90%

SpaceX completed the largest tech IPO in history under ticker SPCX. Zephirin Group initiated coverage with Buy rating and $310 price target — the first formal analyst coverage. Insider lockups (Musk minimum 1 year) suppress near-term selling pressure. Index inclusion (Nasdaq, Russell) is forcing institutional accumulation. Post-IPO rally stretched over three consecutive sessions with retail and institutional demand both strong.

What it means: SPCX is a momentum-driven name, not fundamentally driven. The structural floor thesis: Elon aiming to establish a permanent $1.5-2 trillion market cap floor. Index funds are forced buyers regardless of valuation. The bear case trigger: price below $185-190. Upside target: $222-230. Key risk: the only company worth over $1 trillion that loses billions annually. SpaceX also acquired Cursor (Anysphere) for $60B in stock — an enterprise AI expansion signal.

RKLB ASTS
Confirmed
Analyst: Zephirin Group — Buy, $310 PT

AI coding agents move from demo to production use in enterprise software development. GitHub Copilot Workspace, Cursor's composer mode, and Cognition's Devin handle end-to-end feature development for well-defined tasks. Controlled enterprise studies show 20-40% productivity gains for specific task categories. Human review remains mandatory for security-sensitive paths and architectural decisions.

What it means: Microsoft captures this wave through GitHub (Copilot) and Azure (inference). The productivity gains are real but the timeline to autonomous development without human review is 2028+. Models that can verify their own work (formal reasoning) are the next unlock: watch DeepMind research publication cadence.

MSFT GOOGL NVDA
Confident
Leader: MSFT · 85% vs GOOGL 85% · NVDA 75% · +1 more

First factory-floor pilot deployments of humanoid robots. Tesla Optimus, Figure AI, and Boston Dynamics Atlas are targeting automotive and logistics environments. The enabling breakthrough is multi-modal foundation models that allow rapid task acquisition from human demonstration rather than manual programming. NVIDIA's Isaac Sim is the dominant training environment. First-generation units are priced at $30,000-$50,000.

What it means: Tesla is the most direct equity play. NVIDIA is the infrastructure play: every humanoid being trained on simulation runs on NVIDIA GPUs. The 18-month data from these pilots (task success rates, uptime, maintenance cost) will determine whether this transitions to mass production or remains a high-cost niche. ABB and Rockwell benefit if humanoids become the standard factory automation interface.

TSLA NVDA HON
Confident
Leader: TSLA · 82% vs NVDA 55% · +1 more

First A14 wafers in risk production. Volume production targeted 2027. Final gate-all-around FinFlex generation before shift to new transistor architectures. High-NA EUV (ASML EXE:5000) is required for A14 patterning. Yield ramp on High-NA tools is the critical path: each EXE:5000 costs over €350 million and takes years to qualify.

What it means: ASML EXE:5000 shipments are the leading indicator. ASML has confirmed multi-unit orders from TSMC and Intel. A14 risk production start validates the High-NA roadmap and is a positive catalyst for ASML's 2027-2029 revenue guidance.

TSM ASML LRCX KLAC
Confident
Leader: TSM · 99% vs ASML 90% · KLAC 75% · LRCX 75% · +3 more

Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have signed long-term nuclear power purchase agreements for data centre load. The Microsoft/Constellation deal (Crane Clean Energy Center, reopened Three Mile Island) is the flagship. SMR (Small Modular Reactor) first plants targeted late 2020s. These deals are not green branding: they are infrastructure procurement driven by grid reliability requirements for always-on 100-500MW data centre loads.

What it means: Constellation Energy (CEG) has locked in long-term PPA revenue at premium rates. GE Vernova (GEV) is the primary BWRX-300 SMR vendor with confirmed orders. The power infrastructure story (Eaton, Quanta) benefits regardless of nuclear's specific role. Uranium miners (CCJ, UUUU) are the commodity play on nuclear expansion.

GEV CEG ETN
Confirmed
Leader: CEG · 95%

True 3D chip stacking without interposers reaches pilot volumes. TSMC SoIC-X and Intel Foveros Direct are the leading implementations. This approach doubles effective transistor density versus planar chiplet approaches by eliminating the interposer entirely and bonding wafers directly. Critical enabler for post-2nm scaling where traditional planar area scaling is exhausted.

What it means: This technology is the most direct path to continuing Moore's Law gains when 2D scaling stops. TSMC leadership here is not guaranteed: Intel Foveros has demonstrated comparable bond pitch. AMAT's wafer bonding equipment is required for both approaches. This is a 2027-2030 catalyst, not 2026.

TSM INTC AMAT
Researching
Leader: TSM · 99% vs AMAT 78% · INTC 60% · +4 more

Chain-of-thought reasoning becomes the baseline expectation across all frontier models. Inference compute costs per task are dropping dramatically as model efficiency improves, but total compute spend is increasing because usage expands faster than efficiency gains. The "more efficient = less compute" assumption has been consistently wrong throughout AI history.

What it means: NVIDIA wins in both the efficiency scenario (still needs GPUs for inference) and the volume scenario (more queries = more GPUs). The question shifts to which company can run reasoning inference at lowest cost: favouring hyperscalers with proprietary training infrastructure (Google TPU, AWS Trainium) for their own workloads, while NVIDIA remains the vendor of choice for third parties.

MSFT GOOGL NVDA AMD
Confident
Leader: MSFT · 85% vs GOOGL 85% · NVDA 75% · +1 more

AWS Graviton, Apple M-series derivatives, Qualcomm Cloud AI, and NVIDIA Grace push ARM architecture past 40% of new data centre CPU deployments. The performance-per-watt advantage of ARM over x86 is well-documented in cloud workloads. Intel's market share loss in cloud CPUs is structural, not cyclical.

What it means: ARM Holdings benefits from royalties on every ARM CPU shipped regardless of who manufactures it. The royalty per chip is increasing as CPU complexity grows. This is the most durable royalty stream in semiconductors: analogous to QUALCOMM's handset royalties in the mobile era.

ARM QCOM NVDA AMZN
Confident
Leader: NVDA · 90% vs AMZN 80% · ARM 80% · +3 more

Silicon photonics replaces copper SerDes for in-rack and rack-to-rack interconnects in AI data centres. Co-packaged optics (CPO): optical engines packaged directly alongside compute dies: delivers 4-8x bandwidth density improvement and 30-50% power reduction over pluggable optical modules. This technology is the single highest-impact bottleneck node in our research graph: more downstream technologies depend on it than any other single node. Unlocks 34 downstream technology categories including next-generation cluster architectures, quantum networking, and photonic computing.

What it means: Lumentum (LITE) and Coherent (COHR) supply the laser chips and photonic integrated circuits at the heart of CPO. Both are priced as cyclical hardware vendors rather than structural bottleneck incumbents. The hyperscaler production qualification (expected 2026-2027) is the catalyst that shifts the supply chain. NVIDIA benefits from higher bandwidth enabling larger clusters.

NVDA INTC MRVL TSM
Researching
Leader: MRVL · 78% vs NVDA 70% · INTC 60% · +5 more

TSMC Arizona Fab 21 (2nm process) reaching significant volume. First on-shore advanced node production for US national security customers. Fab 21 Phase 2 (1.4nm/A14) targeting 2027-2028 start. The Arizona fabs represent a historic shift in semiconductor supply chain geography: the first advanced node fabs built on US soil in decades.

What it means: Arizona production provides TSMC access to CHIPS Act subsidies (~$6.6B direct grants) and de-risks geopolitical Taiwan exposure for US government customers. Cost structure is higher than Taiwan but government contracts are cost-plus. Apple and NVIDIA are confirmed customers. Applied Materials and Lam Research supply fabs equipment to Arizona exactly as they do Taiwan.

TSM AMAT LRCX
Confident
Leader: TSM · 99% vs AMAT 78% · LRCX 75% · +4 more

Technologies by Theme

🌐 AI Compute Infrastructure
NVDA AMD AVGO
GPU clusters, AI ASICs, and reasoning models are the demand signal. NVIDIA's CUDA moat makes hardware switching prohibitively expensive. AMD MI300X is the only credible alternative at scale.
🖥 Advanced Semiconductors
TSM ASML AMAT LRCX KLAC
2nm in production, 1.4nm in risk production. TSMC and ASML hold effective monopolies at the leading edge. WFE (wafer fab equipment) order books confirm $300B+ capex cycle.
⚡ Power & Energy
ETN PWR GEV CEG
The most underloved AI derivative. Transformers, switchgear, and grid interconnection are the binding constraint on new data centre capacity in the US. Multi-year backlog, pricing power.
🤖 Humanoid Robotics
TSLA NVDA HON
Pilot deployments live in 2026. 18 months of real production data will determine whether this transitions to mass production. NVIDIA powers all training via Isaac Sim. Tesla is the most direct equity play.
😎 Memory
MU
HBM3E is the bandwidth solution for AI training. Each B200 GPU ships with 192GB HBM3E. Micron is qualifying to take significant share from SK Hynix. HBM margins are substantially higher than DRAM commodity.
🌐 Software Platforms
MSFT GOOGL
AI software agents and hyperscaler cloud are the monetisation layer. Microsoft owns GitHub (Copilot) + Azure + OpenAI equity. Google owns DeepMind (AlphaFold, AlphaProof) + GCP + Waymo.
⚛ Quantum Computing
IBM IONQ GOOGL
Google Willow proved error rates improve with qubit count: a foundational result. IBM roadmap targets 100,000 qubits by 2033. Fault-tolerant QC is a 2030s event. Treat quantum stocks as venture-style positions sized accordingly.
🔗 Interconnects
MRVL INTC
Silicon photonics is the single highest-impact bottleneck in our research graph: 34 downstream technologies depend on it. Co-packaged optics commercial deployment is targeted 2028. Lumentum and Coherent supply the optical components.

Investment Implications

  • TSMC and ASML remain the two most irreplaceable companies in the global chip supply chain
  • Power infrastructure (ETN, GEV, PWR) is the most underloved AI derivative play
  • Memory (MU) enters a multi-year upcycle on HBM demand
  • ARM royalty model scales with every AI server chip shipped
